correctness.rationale: Exact Haar construction U=G(G*G)^(-1/2) holds for real/complex two-frames. On a simultaneous high-probability covariance event, all n edge lengths satisfy (1-delta)T_i <= n ell_i <= (1+delta)T_i with delta=O(sqrt(log n/n)). The independent row norms are chi-square_2 or Gamma(2,1); their explicit joint order-statistic formula yields Exp/Rayleigh and Gumbel independent limits. Gaussian rare-bin Laplace functionals give the marked independent Poisson processes. Differentiated CDFs and the common sandwich establish the claimed compact-threshold O(log(n)^(3/2)/sqrt(n)) comparison. The packaged script verifies finite identities and samples, not the infinite convergence.

value.rationale: The probability of extreme very short or very long edges controls practical sampling of geometrically balanced closed random polygons, and the closure constraint makes naive all-edge independence nontrivial. The theorem jointly quantifies both extremes, their edge-index point patterns and an all-edge threshold approximation with rate in both real and complex Haar models. It resolves a specific approximate-independence issue in the motivating source rather than merely computing another one-edge beta marginal.
